evidence.claim: The 2022 report says Pakistan faced serious human rights issues including arbitrary killings, enforced disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, political prisoners, restrictions on expression and assembly, and widespread impunity for abuses.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 report says Pakistan faced serious human rights issues including arbitrary killings, enforced disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, political prisoners, restrictions on expression and assembly, and widespread impunity for abuses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government human-rights report summarizing the year's record with detailed attribution.
evidence.period_fit: Covers the exact 2022 period, including the Sharif-led government from April onward.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to the Sharif government, though some problems predated him and security agencies retained substantial autonomy.
contrary_evidence: The same summary notes a constitutional parliamentary transition to Sharif rather than an immediate breakdown of formal civilian institutions.

evidence.claim: The National Assembly passed the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Bill, 2022 to criminalize torture, custodial death, and custodial rape by public officials and to let the National Commission for Human Rights and the FIA register complaints.
evidence.title: Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Bill, 2022 sails through NA
evidence.excerpt: The National Assembly passed the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Bill, 2022 to criminalize torture, custodial death, and custodial rape by public officials and to let the National Commission for Human Rights and the FIA register complaints.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official state newswire reporting a passed government bill with concrete remedial mechanisms.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Sharif-era reform effort, though implementation quality remains unknown.
contrary_evidence: Passing a bill does not by itself prove reduced abuse or effective enforcement.

evidence.claim: The report says Shahbaz Gill alleged police assaulted and tortured him after his August arrest, and Azam Swati alleged he was stripped and beaten after an October arrest for antimilitary comments.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The report says Shahbaz Gill alleged police assaulted and tortured him after his August arrest, and Azam Swati alleged he was stripped and beaten after an October arrest for antimilitary comments.
evidence.source_locator: torture and custodial abuse section, lines 74-75
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary report captures specific 2022 allegations tied to arrests under the Sharif government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sharif-era policing and detention practices, though the allegations themselves are contested.
contrary_evidence: These are allegations reported by the State Department, not judicial findings in the report itself.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the FIA detained eight people in Punjab after they published criticism of the state on Twitter and described the arrests as part of a repressive crackdown on free expression and opposition supporters.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Immediately release eight people arrested over critical tweets
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the FIA detained eight people in Punjab after they published criticism of the state on Twitter and described the arrests as part of a repressive crackdown on free expression and opposition supporters.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct human-rights advocacy statement with clear date, named agency, and explicit arrest allegation.
evidence.period_fit: Exact April 2022, immediately after Sharif's accession.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Sharif-era enforcement, though the cyberlaw framework itself predated him.
contrary_evidence: The FIA said the arrests were not tied to political opposition parties.

evidence.claim: HRW says government threats and attacks on media continued in 2022, journalists were harassed or detained, critical channels were blocked, and multiple journalists faced charges or threats.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: HRW says government threats and attacks on media continued in 2022, journalists were harassed or detained, critical channels were blocked, and multiple journalists faced charges or threats.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major independent rights report with specific 2022 examples and named journalists.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Sharif-era authorities as government practice, though implementation ran through regulatory and security bodies with partial autonomy.
contrary_evidence: Some of the named incidents involved non-state actors or provincial-level policing, so national-ruler attribution is not uniform.

evidence.claim: HRW says violence against women and girls remained widespread, the government did little to stop child and forced marriage, and at least seven transgender women were killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2022 while minority communities remained vulnerable to abuse.
evidence.title: World Report 2023: Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: HRW says violence against women and girls remained widespread, the government did little to stop child and forced marriage, and at least seven transgender women were killed in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2022 while minority communities remained vulnerable to abuse.
evidence.source_locator: women and girls plus gender-identity sections, lines 92-98 and 114-115
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent rights reporting with concrete 2022 findings and multiple vulnerable-group categories.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited social and legal conditions, but the Sharif government is relevant for failure to protect and remediate.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes one positive institutional step in January 2022, the workplace-harassment amendment, which shows the picture was not uniformly negative.

evidence.claim: After the Islamabad High Court said successive chief executives had given tacit approval to enforced disappearances, the federal government formed a seven-member committee under the law minister to deliberate policy, and the PM was briefed on the issue.
evidence.title: Govt forms committee to 'deliberate policy' on enforced disappearances
evidence.excerpt: After the Islamabad High Court said successive chief executives had given tacit approval to enforced disappearances, the federal government formed a seven-member committee under the law minister to deliberate policy, and the PM was briefed on the issue.
evidence.source_locator: Dawn summary of the IHC order and ministry notification
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a formal government notification and court order; direct PM-level ordering is still indirect.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows Sharif's government responding after judicial notice; it does not prove he personally designed the disappearance policy.
contrary_evidence: The underlying practice predates Sharif and the operational actors are not named here.

evidence.claim: NCHR said the IHC treated enforced disappearances as a 'seemingly undeclared tacit policy of the state' and welcomed the court's order holding chief executives and interior ministers, past and present, accountable, while also welcoming the government's committee on the issue.
evidence.title: NCHR Statement on IHC Ruling on Enforced Disappearances
evidence.publisher: National Commission for Human Rights Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: NCHR said the IHC treated enforced disappearances as a 'seemingly undeclared tacit policy of the state' and welcomed the court's order holding chief executives and interior ministers, past and present, accountable, while also welcoming the government's committee on the issue.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statutory human-rights body summarizing the court ruling and government response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for attribution of Sharif's government as the addressed authority; weak for proving personal operational direction.
contrary_evidence: The statement does not identify which security actors carried out individual disappearances.

evidence.claim: Amnesty reported that families of the disappeared and activists protesting enforced disappearances were met with state violence, intimidation, arbitrary detention, and arrest for peaceful assembly.
evidence.title: Pakistan: Braving the Storm: Enforced disappearances and the right to protest in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty reported that families of the disappeared and activists protesting enforced disappearances were met with state violence, intimidation, arbitrary detention, and arrest for peaceful assembly.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent rights report with a clear 2022 scope and specific abuse pattern.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports a state-abuse pattern under Sharif's term, but it does not by itself prove his personal ordering of each incident.
contrary_evidence: The report attributes the abuses to state forces generally, not to Sharif personally.

evidence.claim: The Islamabad High Court ordered the federal government and interior secretary to appoint an inquiry officer into allegations that PTI leader Shahbaz Gill was tortured in police custody, and ordered SSP-level supervision to ensure no further torture.
evidence.title: IHC orders inquiry into claims of torture on Gill
evidence.excerpt: The Islamabad High Court ordered the federal government and interior secretary to appoint an inquiry officer into allegations that PTI leader Shahbaz Gill was tortured in police custody, and ordered SSP-level supervision to ensure no further torture.
evidence.source_locator: report of the IHC order and the court's directions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Court order summarized by a mainstream local outlet; the underlying court record is the stronger source but was not directly accessible here.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly implicates the police custody chain during Sharif's government, but not a proven personal order by Sharif.
contrary_evidence: Police and government officials denied torture; the dispute remained under inquiry.

evidence.claim: NCHR said its Adiala Jail inquiry found 74% of interviewed inmates alleging torture and 100% reporting financial extortion for access to basic facilities, and the court ordered the report shared with the PM and cabinet for immediate action against responsible public servants.
evidence.title: Press Release: NCHR Inquiry Report on Custodial Torture at Central Jail (Adiala), Rawalpindi
evidence.publisher: National Commission for Human Rights Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: NCHR said its Adiala Jail inquiry found 74% of interviewed inmates alleging torture and 100% reporting financial extortion for access to basic facilities, and the court ordered the report shared with the PM and cabinet for immediate action against responsible public servants.
evidence.source_locator: paragraphs describing the inquiry findings and court directions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official inquiry report announcement with concrete findings and a court-ordered response chain.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for prison administration under the federal government; still indirect for naming Sharif as the actor behind abuse.
contrary_evidence: The report describes jail conditions and responsible public servants, not a personal PM order.

evidence.claim: President Arif Alvi wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressing deep concern over harassment of journalists, citing arrests, beatings, harassment, and sedition cases meant to create fear and terror, and urging immediate remedial action and protection from security agencies.
evidence.title: Alvi concerned over treatment of journalists
evidence.excerpt: President Arif Alvi wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressing deep concern over harassment of journalists, citing arrests, beatings, harassment, and sedition cases meant to create fear and terror, and urging immediate remedial action and protection from security agencies.
evidence.source_locator: Dawn summary of the president's letter
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report of a direct written notice to Sharif from the head of state.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is direct notice to Sharif and his government; it still does not prove he personally directed the harassment.
contrary_evidence: The letter is a warning and request, not proof of authorial control over every abuse.

evidence.claim: NCHR launched a complaint cell for women journalists after a consultative meeting with women journalists from across Pakistan, citing online violence, harassment, attack risks, and censorship against women reporters.
evidence.title: NCHR launches complaint cell for women journalists
evidence.excerpt: NCHR launched a complaint cell for women journalists after a consultative meeting with women journalists from across Pakistan, citing online violence, harassment, attack risks, and censorship against women reporters.
evidence.source_locator: article body describing the launch and the consultative meeting
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting of an official human-rights initiative with specific abuse descriptions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Useful as evidence of a documented abuse environment and institutional response; the PM link remains indirect unless paired with the president's letter.
contrary_evidence: The article does not establish direct PM-level authorship of the abuse campaigns.

evidence.claim: NCHR's minority report said nearly half of reserved minority posts were vacant, 80% of non-Muslims in filled posts were in BPS 01-04, and the Ministry of Human Rights sent letters to provincial chief secretaries directing them to protect minority rights.
evidence.title: NCHR launches fact finding report on minority rights
evidence.excerpt: NCHR's minority report said nearly half of reserved minority posts were vacant, 80% of non-Muslims in filled posts were in BPS 01-04, and the Ministry of Human Rights sent letters to provincial chief secretaries directing them to protect minority rights.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official news service reporting a government-linked rights report and subsequent ministry action to provinces.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for provincial policy action under Sharif's federal government; weak for proving personal day-to-day management.
contrary_evidence: The report reflects longstanding structural discrimination and does not isolate Sharif as the sole cause.

unresolved_gaps: No independent 2022 evidence of a Sharif-chaired NCA session or any doctrine, custody, or command-and-control reform.
No direct evidence of Sharif's handling of dual-use, proliferation, cyber, biosecurity, or AI-risk policy in 2022.
The April 2022 Afghanistan strike allegation remains unresolved by an independent finding or clear attribution chain.
No formal ceasefire or settlement output with India or Afghanistan beyond public diplomacy and border-management statements.
Primary court orders or audit findings on the Ramzan Sugar Mills and Ashiana matters are still needed to separate allegations from a durable personal-nexus finding.
The appointment/favoritism question still lacks stronger evidence about whether key personnel choices reflected merit or protection of insiders.
